subject: fennec
pitch: A fennec fox kit standing alert on a little sand dune at dusk. Enormous satin ears lined in pale peach, cream fur warming to sandy gold along its back, a fluffy tail with a smudge of black at the tip, and big dark eyes with a tiny white sparkle. Its paws are a touch oversized, like it hasn't grown into them yet, and it wears a woven leather collar with a small brass bell.
reasoning:
I'm planning the scene layout—a dune with a fox kit standing on top, working out realistic proportions like a ~0.3m body length and short legs scaled to fennec fox sizing.

I'm sketching the dune's lathe profile for a flattened mound shape, then mapping out skeleton joint coordinates for the fox: hips, spine curve, chest, neck, and head positions using a catmull chain anchored at a root hip joint.

I'm tapering the body radius toward the chest and neck, then sweeping the spine path with those radii. For coloring, I'm going with a countershaded coat, warming from cream on the belly to sandy gold along the back using a gradient.

Now I'm setting up the legs with inverse kinematics, placing shoulder and foot targets and checking the limb lengths so the legs bend naturally rather than staying rigid.

For the hind leg I'll settle on a slightly folded crouched pose with three segments ending roughly vertical. For the foreleg I'm using two segments bending back at the elbow, with the root tucked inside the body radius so it emerges naturally, and I'm picking a leg sweep radius around 0.016-0.02 tapering down.

I'm planning oversized cream-colored paws with a flattened elliptical scale, placed so they sit just above the ground plane, plus small toe bumps and maybe dark claw details using simple sphere geometry at the tip joint.

Now I'm moving to the head region: a small skull sphere scaled for the fennec's compact proportions, with a tapered snout built from frustum shapes for upper and lower jaw, a dark nose tip, and large dark eye spheres positioned on the front sides of the head.

I'm working out the eye geometry more precisely -- almond-shaped dark spheres with tiny white sparkle highlights offset toward the upper-outer front, calculating local coordinates relative to the head's radius so the eyes sit properly on the skull surface.

Now I'm designing the fennec ears: large pointed leaf-shaped outlines extruded with thickness, sized around 0.13 tall and 0.06 wide, positioned at the top sides of the head and tilted outward.

Working through the handedness check, I confirm the thickness direction stays forward regardless of which side the ear is mirrored to, so the outline stays symmetric either way. Now I'm sketching the actual ear outline coordinates, tracing points from the base up to the pointed tip and back down.

Finishing the ear outline and adding an inner lining layer in a peach tone, scaled down and offset forward along the thickness axis so it sits nested inside the outer gold shape.

I'm planning cheek tufts as cream spike cones angled back-outward, skipping fur card textures in favor of geometric spikes for cost. For the tail, I'm sketching a fluffy chain sweep with a thick radius plus added spike tufts, working out the joint points from hips down and back.

I'm nudging the tail curve so it hovers just above the dune surface instead of clipping into it, adjusting the final joint heights to get a slight upward hang at the tip while keeping it close to the ground.

Now I'm reshaping the dune into a broader, flatter mound with a gentle plateau, checking that the tail and foot positions still land correctly on its sloped surface at each radius.

For texture, I'm thinking about adding subtle sand ripple details and mottled coloring rather than heavy decoration—keeping it simple with a few scattered pebbles instead of grass tufts, and considering thin arc sweeps across the dune surface to suggest wind-blown ripples with a slightly lighter shade.

Now I'm working out the fox's overall proportions, checking that the ear height relative to head size and shoulder height still reads as an oversized fennec-style ear on a small seated body.

For the tail, I'm setting up a black tip using color bands near the end of the sweep, defining a tapering radius profile along its length with rounded caps, and chaining it to the hips with four segments for added fluffiness.

I'll use this tail paint function for the spike and band coloring, with black tips near the last quarter of the tail length. For the body, I'm planning fur tufts scattered on the chest and back using cream cones filtered by surface normal and position, plus a woven leather collar looped around the neck.

Writing the collar weave pattern...

I'm trying to pin down which spine joint should anchor the collar loop, considering the chest and neck joints and how the head sphere might overlap the neck. I think using a point partway along the chain near the neck, with the frame's tangent direction, would place the loop correctly across the neck.

Now I'm figuring out where to place the brass bell on the collar front-bottom — offsetting from the chain point downward and forward, then projecting that onto the nearest point on the collar sweep surface to attach a small brass sphere there.

For the slit and ring details, I'm thinking through the trickier geometry: a small dark box for the slit, a thin ring or torus for decoration, all needing to be oriented correctly relative to the hit point's surface normal rather than just placed at default orientation.

Adding whiskers, nose, facial fur patches, and jawbone structure with a hierarchical joint setup parented to the head...

Adding cheek tufts with backward-pointing spikes using cream color, keeping head spheres gold-cream with shared coat gradient, and now thinking through whether legs should go gold on the upper segment and cream below.

I'm settling on pale tan for the leg color and a lighter cream for the paws, considering skipping the dark foreleg stripe seen on real fennecs, and sizing hind paws larger with a flattened, elongated sphere shape.

For toes, I'll add three small cream spheres plus claws spaced along the front of each paw, keeping the overall paw part count manageable, and I'm checking that the bone chain for each leg includes a tip joint to attach the paw to.

Working out the joint naming scheme now: fore legs use shoulder/elbow/wrist with a tip, while hind legs need hip/knee/hock/ankle to cover the extra segment, making sure point counts match span counts plus the tip joint on each side.

I'm tapering leg radii with the thigh thicker for hind limbs, positioning legs relative to body half-width so roots sit inside the torso, and shaping the body sweep with a hip bulge profile running from narrower shoulders to a wider hip before tapering toward the head.

For the spine, I'm sharing one chain to cover the back and neck, with hips acting as the root joint that also parents the tail chain. For fur, I'm scattering chest fluff by filtering hit points on the body surface by height and normal direction, using cream-colored cones, and sticking with simple spheres for the eyes rather than more complex geometry.

Now I'm adding small cream fringe tufts inside each ear, placing three spikes per ear near the ear base using local directions relative to the ear joint, angled upward and slightly forward with varying horizontal offsets.

A subtle dark rim on the eye spheres, no brow detail, with the pose set alert and ears up, head tilted slightly upward. Now I'm starting the actual build function, importing the geometry helpers and setting up the builder with named colors before beginning the lathe profile for the body base.

I realize I need a root hips joint established before attaching the dune prop, so the dune will follow the hips bone rather than floating unparented. I'm working out the lathe outline points for the dune shape, moving outward from the central axis with decreasing radius values to form a smooth mound.

For the sand texture, I'm layering stripe patterns over a mottled base with varying colors and widths to get a natural dusky sand look, then planning to scatter pebbles across the dune's surface.

Now I'm setting up the spine path with catmull-rom splines across the points, then writing the leg-building code with limb functions positioned per side and bend directions passed as vectors...

Still writing limb code...

Working out the sparkle position on the eye surface and verifying the distance math checks out, then sizing the eye shape itself with a scale factor to make it appear bigger.

I'm also adding a dark eyeliner rod connecting the eye to the nose along the muzzle surface, and setting up whisker placement with three strands per side radiating outward from a base point near the muzzle.

Now I'm working out the collar as a swept shape along a loop path across the body, using a box-section sweep with bone weights blended smoothly along the spine for natural deformation.

Then I'm positioning a brass bell by finding the nearest point on the collar surface to a point offset below the neck, and attaching a torus geometry there with brass coloring and orientation taken from that hit point's frame.

Writing ear geometry code...

Picking out the rest of the palette and setting up the coat gradient for a cream-to-gold countershaded blend, with the ears shifting to a satin tan and the tail paint toggling between black, cream, and gold based on position. That covers the coloring logic, so I'm ready to write the final code.
